APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF SEPTEMBER 3, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:04 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  4-0 (Councilmember Ancona absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:05 pm.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:04 pm.

  City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items
  4.1 through 4.4.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:
  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.
  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.
  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Charles Hoffman – On September 22, 2019 from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm the El Monte
  Historical Society will be hosting its quarterly tea. Barbara Romero will be speaking
  about growing up in El Monte.

  Sandra Armenta Lopez – We are having a citizenship clinic on September 14, 2019 from
  9:00 am to 3:00 pm at the Rosemead Community Center and everything is free. We
  invite everyone to come out and participate in this.

  Cosme Jimenez – I would like to congratulate our new City Manager Alma Martinez. I
  want to congratulate her but I think it is going to be hard for her because we need

  3

  miracles. If we do not have stability with the City Manager, we will not have stability for

16.  CITY MANAGER’S AGENDA:

  16.1  Update Regarding Southern California Edison LED Conversion Program.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Can we please go back to the upfront costs?
  There are no upfront costs so if you could go over the financing once again?
  Question in regards to the labor that will be doing the installation is that
  contracted through SCE or does El Monte have a say so in this? Do you know if
  SASCO is a union shop?

  Councilmember Morales – Is there going to be a priority with respect to how the
  lights will be replaced? Are they going to start on the east side of the City, the
  North side, is there a schedule? Does this include all of the streetlights? The

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 3, 2019

  reason why I bring this up is because Chief Reynoso and I attended a
  conference at USC with respect to civic engagement beyond crime data and how
  do you assess to which residents perceive that their community is safe and
  interestingly enough one of the topics that came up was lighting and that
  residents have expressed that residents feel safer when their lights are well lit
  and their community is again provided an environment where it is highly visible.

  Mayor Pro Tem – I would like to recommend I don’t know what the schedule is
  for putting up the lights but sometimes we overlook certain parts of the City so I
  would recommend that we go with the darker areas that we have had. I know
  that Mountain View has been a part that sometimes needs us to look at even
  more so now so I would highly recommend to the City Manager or the
  Departments that we take care of these areas because we usually take care of
  northern part of the area faster than others.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – I would like to recommend and hopefully
  Council will support this the project savings on an annual basis should be set
  aside into a special fund so that we can repay whatever it was that we were
  investing. I recognize that you are saying that there are no upfront costs but I
  don’t want us to continue to use this $50,000 or whatever our potential cost
  savings could be that we designate a certain amount of money that gets put in so
  that when it comes time to repay for these lights that we actually have those
  funds and we are not pulling from the General Fund in fact we would be paying
  for it via the cost savings that we have received.

  Mayor Quintero – The savings are embedded in the bill so we are not writing a
  separate check.

16.2  Update Regarding the Joint City Council and Planning Commission Meeting on
  September 17, 2019 at the Grace T. Black Auditorium.

  Mayor Quintero – For those of you who are paying attention we will be adjourning
  this meeting to an Adjourned Regular City Council meeting on September 17,
  2019 at the Grace T. Black Auditorium.

  City Manager – That is exactly what the update is inviting the community and
  also remind the City Council that we will be having a joint meeting with the
  Planning Commission on Tuesday, September 17, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. at the
  Grace T. Black Auditorium.

  Mayor Quintero – Do we have an agenda?

  City Manager – You will be provided and it will be posted.

  Mayor Quintero – Have you had a chance to talk to the City Councilmembers to
  see what items they would like to see on the agenda?

  City Manager – Some of them have been polled and some of them we are still
  working on that. One of the things that is going to be covered is the Garvey
  overlay we will have a presentation.

  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco – I believe there was a notice sent by the City
  Manager’s Office to the Council and we are to submit any items by next week.

  Councilmember Morales – I think that having served on the Planning
  Commission I think that this type of meeting is perfect in the sense of allowing
  the direct communication, to allow an easier process when projects come
  through so that we are all aligned the City Council and Planning Commission so
  that we are all aligned in the vision for our City, the goals for our City and how we
  are going to get through to that vision. Thank you Alma for putting that on the
  calendar I think it is going to be a very important meeting for us to have and I
  think it is going to put us in the right direction with respect to future planning.

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 3, 2019

16.3  Discussion Regarding Events Policy.

16.4  Presentation of the Water and Sewer Budget.

16.5  Discussion Regarding the City Manager’s Spending Authority.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – One of the things that is important in this
  regard and appreciate you bringing this to us Madam City Manager is the idea of
  a quarterly reports but considering that there was a budget that was passed that
  was $834 in the black according to your projections I think it is really critical that
  this year we manage and maintain a spending our we stop the spending that is
  not bearing fruit. If the Council has the availability to take a look and say look I
  appreciate we spent these dollars and this is the return on our investment this is
  something that is new that we have not seen previously from our other City
  Managers that we are instituting now especially in the idea that this budget is so
  tight that we need to be vigilant with each dollar. I appreciate that and I don’t
  know if I am open quite yet so you are going to have to do some convincing to
  upping the spending authority but I am open to hearing your quarterly reports.

  Mayor Quintero – This is going to have to come back to us in the form of a code
  amendment right. So I look forward to that. The only thing I would say to the
  Council is particularly when it comes to the CIP projects and the street projects
  we are not deploying them quickly enough and over the last year or so I don’t
  know how many authorizations we have given to do street work and candidly
  speaking I know we have the resources to do it and this community has been
  asking us to do more work there so we need to do that. I think that whatever can
  help facilitate that obviously within limits and all of this is with the authorization
  and reporting that comes with it I can tell you that we cut down the spending
  authority of the City Manager about 9 years ago because there were contracts
  that were being led that we didn’t even know about and it was very frustrating so
  look forward to seeing that proposal.

  City Manager – Thank you Mayor I just wanted to remind the Council again that it
  takes 7 to 10 months to design a street to get everything so it takes a while to get
  shovels on the ground so the sooner you can engage people at the low level
  prices for design, appraisals, consulting and things of that nature the sooner we
  can these projects and the money deployed for the CIP Projects.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – It is also very important though to follow the
  money and understand if there is a typical protocol that should be follow for the
  presence of transparency then we should be following that and it should be
  brought to the Council continuously so that we can review it and continue to
  move forward and support with the CIP but we also need to know who is doing
  business within our City. That is key, who is doing business in our City and that is
  where this is critical.

16.6  Consideration to Receive and File a Report on the Traffic Safety Committee and
  Vision Zero Advisory Committee, and Authorization for a Code Amendment and
  Allocation of Resources for the Preparation of the Vision Zero Action Plan.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve to receive and file a report on Traffic Safety Committee
  and Vision Zero Advisory Committee;
  2. Authorize a Code Amendment to combine Traffic Safety Committee and
  Vision Zero Advisory Committee and establish either: (1) a Mobility Safety
  Commission; or (2) a Mobility Safety Committee; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to allocate resources for the preparation of the
  Vision Zero Action Plan.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 3, 2019

Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

David Diaz – I have been fortunate enough to participate in the El Monte Vision
Zero process, I have spearheaded a lot of efforts over the course of the last five
years. I am here to express my support in consolidating the two committees
because I do feel that there is overlap in their function. However, I am here to
express my support for a remix, a combination of the two ideas in particular
because in the recommendation for the Mobility Safety Commission its adopted
with only recommendation of only having City staff participate and in its current
function as the El Monte Vision Zero Committee it is a combination of City staff
and community base organizations which have included San Gabriel Valley, Day
One, First Five LA, Investing at Place at Times, and other groups so to Braden’s
point about we want to make sure that there is transparency I think a good
